label: STL Atlas Lite air-blown 12F, 2.3 mm
notes: The duct cable: twelve fibres in one 2.3 mm gel-filled unitube, installed by blowing into a single or bundled microduct - the product a route measured over an imported duct graph actually buys, which the catalogue did not stock (its other 12F rows are outdoor loose-tube on a 2 km drum and an indoor riser on a 4.1 km reel). The sheet offers the same design in G.652.D, G.657.A1 or G.657.A2; this row prices the G.657.A2 build, because a blown cable is bent hard at a chamber and the bend-insensitive grade is the one sold for it. Attenuation here is the sheet's MAXIMUM cabled attenuation, not a typical: 0.35 dB/km at 1310 nm and 0.23 dB/km at 1550 nm, so a budget built on this row is a worst case rather than a best one. The sheet publishes no 1490 nm figure, and a PON downstream is budgeted at 1490; the 0.26 dB/km in this row is the straight line between the two published maxima - 0.23 + (0.35 - 0.23) x (1550 - 1490) / (1550 - 1310) = 0.26 - and is nobody's measurement, so it must not be read as a vendor figure. `drumM` is the sheet's standard length multiple, 4 km, and it rounds in 4 km steps: a 5.5 km duct run bills 8 km of this cable where 2 km drums bill 6 km. `use` deliberately carries no drop: an air-blown cable is not a house drop and must never be selected for a sub-300 m span. Replace all three attenuation figures with the test report of the cable actually purchased before ordering.
